page: Google Cloud Platform n1-standard-96 is a general-purpose virtual machine offering 96 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 48 physical Intel Xeon cores via simultaneous multithreading. It provides 360.0 GB of system memory, yielding 3.75 GB per vCPU, supported by a 38 MB L3 cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 KB L1d cache. The x86_64 architecture incorporates instruction extensions including AVX and AVX-512F alongside cryptographic AES acceleration, while lacking newer extensions such as AMX or AVX-512 VNNI. The instance includes no bundled local storage and features zero GPUs.

Benchmark evaluations demonstrate a clear division between single-threaded throughput and parallel processing capabilities. Single-core tests such as stress-ng and Geekbench register within the bottom 25th percentile, reflecting the older microarchitecture of the N1 generation. Conversely, highly parallelized testing demonstrates strong throughput, with stress-ng multi-core performance scaling into the top quartile alongside 62.03 million Redis SET operations per second. Memory throughput is also strong across large read blocks at 213.36 GB/s and write blocks at 92.34 GB/s. However, sequential single-threaded decompression and token generation for LLMs remain constrained.

From an infrastructure efficiency perspective, the n1-standard-96 offers substantial aggregate CPU capacity and memory density for large-scale enterprise deployments, but the tradeoff lies in per-core execution speeds and the absence of native local storage disks or bundled public IPv4 addresses. Network or persistent storage must be attached independently. The instance is suited for multi-threaded distributed caching, large web serving farms, batch compilation tasks, and parallel backend services rather than single-threaded or modern AI generation tasks.
description: Google Cloud Platform n1-standard-96 is a general-purpose virtual machine equipped with 96 dedicated vCPUs derived from 48 physical Intel Xeon cores running on the x86_64 architecture. The system provides 360.0 GB of RAM (3.75 GB per vCPU) with 38 MB of L3 cache, supporting AVX and AVX-512F instructions. It does not include local disk storage or GPU accelerators, relying entirely on remote storage volumes. Benchmark data shows weak single-core execution across Geekbench and compression tasks, contrasted with strong multi-core scaling in stress-ng and memory bandwidth testing that exceeds 213 GB/s on large uncached reads. Additionally, in-memory key-value processing reaches 62.03 million operations per second on Redis SET workloads. The n1-standard-96 offers high compute density across dozens of cores, presenting an operational tradeoff between total multi-threaded throughput and modest individual core speed. This instance is best suited for concurrent backend enterprise applications, memory caching pools, and distributed web serving.
